key_insight: LLM-discovered heuristics directly construct promising vehicle-routing subproblems, matching neural policies in-distribution and outperforming them on large-scale out-of-distribution instances.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers logistics optimization teams interpretable subproblem-selection rules that may generalize beyond the routing instances used during development.
method: Use an LLM to automatically design and refine subproblem-selection heuristics.
Apply the generated heuristics to directly construct subproblems within large-scale capacitated vehicle routing problems.
Optimize the selected subproblems using solvers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparable in-distribution performance and better out-of-distribution performance than neural network-based policies, but provides no numerical results or benchmark sizes.
watch_item: Validate heuristic robustness and end-to-end computational cost on operational routing data before deployment.
paper_title: Revisiting Learning to Delegate: LLM Discovered Heuristics for Large-Scale Vehicle Routing
